Amazon Basics Standby UPS 600VA 360W Surge Protector Battery Power Backup - 8 Outlets, Black I was quite pleased with this UPS when I received it, and bought a couple more in different sizes. I used this with my desktop computer, to bridge the 2-3 minutes it takes between the main power going off and my generator kicking on automatically. It did that job perfectly for about two years, but recently just stopped providing backup power. The computer thinks the battery is fine, and is charging, but with any loss of supply power, this thing just fails to provide the backup power and the computer essentially crashes. I suspect that either the battery isn't good or (more likely) the cutover circuitry isn't functioning properly.

I decided to switch to a TrippLite UPS instead (the AVR series): it gives you a much better system for just a few extra bucks.

text_fidelity_a: Linksys LGS308MP Business Poe+ Smart 8 Port Gigabit Network Switch (130W),Black Pretty much a plug and play device; 1 minute to install.  There is supposed to be a configuration program that you can access, but I wasn't able to do so with the IP address given in the instructions.  It wasn't necessary anyway, as the device functions just fine on a simple network without any additional configuration.  There are two things I didn't like about it compared to my old switch, that I was replacing.  First of all, it is a bit larger than my old switch at 8 1/2 inches long compared to my old one that is only 6 1/2 inches.  Also, the power supply is considerably larger at 6 inches long and 3 inches wide and 1 inch thick.  My old switch uses only a large plug that is 1 3/4 x 1 3/4 x 1 1/4.  The second thing I didn't like is that there are no indicator lights to show the functioning ports.  My old switch has lights for each port that is working, which is nice.  You may prefer not to have any lights and if so, this Linksys switch may be to your liking.  Note: there is a disc included with documentation, but I didn't find it to be of any particular use.  On the plus side, this does appear to be a quality, heavy duty switch, so might be well suited for a commercial application (such as in an unattended area, like a computer room in a large business).  It appears to weigh nearly twice what my old switch did, so it is solid.  I have used Linksys products before and found them to be good quality with no issues.  You can buy a cheaper switch that is smaller and does essentially the same thing at a considerably lower price, but you most likely won't get the same quality as you would with this switch.  Also this switch does apparently have a POE (power over internet) feature and if you need that, you also might want to get this.  I don't see a need for POE in my configuration.  Possibly overkill for typical home office, but if you want a good quality switch, it might be worth the extra cost (or not).
text_fidelity_b: Linksys LGS308MP Business Poe+ Smart 8 Port Gigabit Network Switch (130W),Black

text_fidelity_a:
Koss 155524 UR40 Collapsible Over-Ear Headphones ...and after 13 years of heavy use, I was curious... here's my old headphones!

I went looking, because I like them so much all this time!

A couple things.

The mesh head thing- it only stayed on a couple years. They headphones worked better without it anyhow I think. Smoother on my hair. Which has a fine texture, and is a bit frizzy- lots of fine short pieces. Sometimes the foldable joints catch in them. This happens on earrings, necklaces, other headphones and other things as well. No more on this product really. Function of having fine curly hair.

Sound has always been fantastic. I love the sound and am sad when I send a ton of cash on headphones that don't come close.

They are not a snug fit, but, are soft enough and comfy enough to wear to bed. Because of the tender fabric, it's started to deteriorate on the smooth fake leathery bits. So so soft all this time though. Really to last 13 years, NO COMPLAINTS!!!.

Not snug enough to work out in. Snug enough to casually hike or walk in. They won't just fall right off or anything.

Lightweight. Easy to make a pouch or toss them into a ziplock freezer quart bag to travel and keep them in your pack or bag more tidily.

I would agree with most reviews. I tend to consider the cables 'supple' instead of 'flimsy'-- and this is an important difference! Supple cables don't just out at awkward angles and get caught on as much stuff. You can keep your music device in your pocket and the cable stays nicely under your coat or shirt and bends where you need it to stay and likes being there rather than tugging intself back in to the shape it wants to be in like a stiffer cable.

These are one of the few products I would give 10 stars to if I could.

And I still would after 13 years!!!!!!

Oh,

Actually they still work fine too. Really. I just noticed they are really a little fiddly nowadays because I used them so much, and was wondering if they still made them.

It's a bit disturbing that amazon remembered I bought them so long ago, though. I'm starting to hope Amazon never holds a grudge against me, cause they never forget!!
text_fidelity_b: Koss 155524 UR40 Collapsible Over-Ear Headphones

text_fidelity_a:
Cambridge Soundworks OontZ Angle 3XL Ultra Bluetooth Speaker - Portable Bluetooth Speakers I found it 'dark' and muffled at first. After putting an equalizer in front of it (I used the Windows 7 Equalizer APO 1.2.1, which has it's own graphic equalizer to play around with, and is free), I could tweak the response so that the speaker sounds very high fidelity and even across the frequency range. I am including a screengrab of the equalizer settings I use. As you can see it just needs a bit of tweaking to make it sound it's best. The volume is more than sufficient, but you need to put the speaker volume up high and adjust the volume from your computer or phone. Otherwise, there is a tendency to putting the volume up too high on the phone or computer and over driving the speaker, which will make it sound really distorted.

I spent half the day playing it at roughly 1/3 volume without it running out of power. I take it with me to work, and out on the porch. It's very versatile, but bigger and heavier than most bluetooth portable speakers. It's the price you pay for deep bass, and high quality drivers. If sound is most important to you, go with this. They can also be paired, which must sound very very good indeed.
text_fidelity_b: Cambridge Soundworks OontZ Angle 3XL Ultra Bluetooth Speaker - Portable Bluetooth Speakers

Logitech 910000153 V220 Cordless Optical Mouse for Notebooks [[VIDEOID:c6148faf689d084cd73b4a5362755ed1]] Just playing around with my first ever video review, so please bear with me.

The V220 is a pretty good mouse considering the price tag. It's compact and rugged looking, with rubber pads at the sides for a good grip.

It only needs one AA battery (Note: the diagram is misleading with regard to the way to put in the battery. You should see the + side when you're closing the top)

You can use it for desktops as well as laptops.

There's storage space for the receiver at the bottom, and once you click it into place, the mouse automatically shuts off.

The ridged rubber wheel is the noisy variety, and goes click, click, click, all the way home.

It comes with no software, but gives you a link to the website where you can get a download to make the mouse do tricks. After the download, you can scroll from side to side, click and roll to zoom, and if you give it a shove, it can even roll over and play dead.

It has a warning light to tell you when your battery needs changing.

It doesn't come with a case or pouch, but looks like it can handle going commando just fine.

In summary, it's a good mouse, but not a great mouse - and well worth the price.

Amanda Richards, October 9, 2007
text_fidelity_b: Logitech 910000153 V220 Cordless Optical Mouse for Notebooks

text_fidelity_a:
Edimax Bluetooth Adapter for PC, BT 5.0 EDR Nano USB Dongle, Fast Transfer, for BT Headphones Headset Speakers Keyboard Mouse, Win 10/11 Plug-n-Play, Linux: 2.6.32-6.2, Mint 21 Plug-n-Play, BT-8500 I use this to stream audio to my TWS headphones so I can listen to music, videos, and audio books while working out or doing projects around the house. I've been using it for about a month now, and I'm pretty satisfied with it.

It worked on plug-in with Manjaro KDE, and integrated with the OS without any additional configuration. It reliably auto-connects and the system even routes audio to it while it is connected, and then restores it to my main headphones when it is not.

Audio quality is decent, about what you would expect from something like this. Not as good as a direct connection obviously, but for most non-critical listening this is perfectly sufficient. Just make sure your headphones support the higher bitrate codecs - I knew mine didn't, but double check to be sure. I have some Bose Soundsport Free headphones which are vented, which is great because I can hear what's going on around the house, but they don't support any advanced codec at all. So I end up with about a 500ms delay on the audio. That's fine for me - if I'm at my desk, I'm using my main headphones anyway, but just be aware.

Range is tricky. With the Soundsports, it's pretty bad, maybe twenty feet in open air, ten feet if there's any obstruction. I have some Sony WF-1000XM4 TWS earbuds and they do better, but only by about 50%. If you are going more than 15ft from the source, you may have issues. However, my system is close to a wireless router and a UPS, so that may be interfering in my case.

Broadly, for this price, I'd recommend this. Sure you can look for higher quality transmitters that go for $50-$100, but until you pull the trigger on that, this should serve your purposes fine.
text_fidelity_b: Edimax Bluetooth Adapter for PC, BT 5.0 EDR Nano USB Dongle, Fast Transfer, for BT Headphones Headset Speakers Keyboard Mouse, Win 10/11 Plug-n-Play, Linux: 2.6.32-6.2, Mint 21 Plug-n-Play, BT-8500

Linksys N300: Wi-Fi Wireless Router, Linksys Connect, Parental Controls, Home Internet, Wireless Devices up to 300 Mbps Transfer Speed (Black) I've been using a Linksys router for years and it never missed a beat (their wireless G model with the two antennas). But, after upgrading my Internet from DSL to cable, I thought a new router would be in order.

Before buying one I searched for reviews from computer and tech magazines/sites. Talk about confusing! I'd read one review that gave a sterling endorsement for a particular router; then another review from another site that gave the same router a horrible review.

Since my router needs are pretty basic (just use it to share Internet access) I concentrated on ease of install issues. In that regard there was consensus about how easy Linksys is to install. So I went with them again, and selected the 1200 model since it gave me all that I wanted/needed at a good price (but, to hedge my bets, I got it at a warehouse club so I could return it easily).

So happy with this router! Installation was SO simple -- if you can plug in a cable you can install this router. But, should you want to tinker with settings, you can also access the full, detailed configuration menu and tweak settings to your heart's content. I think it took me longer to open up the box and unwrap the router and power cord than it took to actually get it to work.

Performance so far has been excellent. I put it on the ground level of my house and have no problems getting a strong signal in the basement and upper level. I did find that it helps to put the router in the middle of the house rather than against a wall for best signal strength throughout the house.

Considering that my Linksys G is still cranking along after several years, I'm reasonably confident (or at least hopeful) that this will last me an equal length of time.

If you're looking for a solid, easy to install single band router, this is it. Highly recommend.
text_fidelity_b: Linksys N300: Wi-Fi Wireless Router, Linksys Connect, Parental Controls, Home Internet, Wireless Devices up to 300 Mbps Transfer Speed (Black)

text_fidelity_a:
Olympus OM-D E-M1 16MP Mirrorless Digital Camera with 3-Inch LCD (Body Only) (Silver w/ Black Trim) I have been shooting Olympus cameras since 1978. I have always loved the lenses. With over 2,000,000 shots on my Olympus E-500 camera, I decided it was time to invest in a new camera.

I was reluctant at first to try the EM-1 for three reasons:
- The format is Micro-Four Thirds, not Four Thirds. I take 99% of my photos in the telephoto range, and that is what Four Thirds was optimized to use. Micro-Four Thirds is geared more towards wide angle lenses.
- The camera is mirrorless and uses an electronic Viewfinder (EVF).
- I have to use a converter to mount my existing Four Thirds lenses, and converters have a very bad history.

Out of the box:
The first thing that you notice when you pull the body out is that it is SOLID. The thing feels like it is built like a tank. I have not tried the "splashproof" and other claims, but just holding this body I can believe them. The camera fits well in my hand. My hands are a little large, and my pinky occasionally slides off the bottom. I may buy the grip/extra battery holder later if this proves to be a problem. YMMV.

Using Four Thirds lenses:
I have no Micro Four Thirds lenses and a lot invested in Four Thirds lenses, so using them was a key issue. Olympus has 1/17 or 1 MP of the sensor dedicated to phase detection auto focus, the only type of auto focus that will work with these lenses. I find that the system works very well. Focusing is fast and accurate.

Mounting the converter is easy, as expected. Once mounted, you use a button on the side to release the lens. This is a learning issue since I still normally hit the lens release button on the camera body. I anticipate little real problems with this since as soon as I try to put the cover on the back of the lens I realize my error.

Balance with the 12-60 mm Four Thirds lens is excellent. Holding the lens by the zoom collar, the weight is only slightly behind my left hand. I only have to support the body lightly with my right hand. I personally like that balance. Longer lenses like the 70-300 are also well balanced.

EVF:
I have used a mirrored SLR since 1978 and a rangefinder 35 mm camera and 126 film P&S cameras before that. As you might guess, I favor a direct view to see what I am shooting. EVF have issues with resolution and lag when moving to a different point of interest or following a subject, especially in low light.

The EVF has turned out to be great. I really like Olympus' implementation. There is some lag, but it is generally minimal. The "What You See Is What You Get" is a big plus in my book. Adjust the exposure compensation or manual exposure settings, and the view in the EVF changes to reflect what the image will look like. It is not perfect, but it gets 95%+ of what you will actually get. The display of settings is bright, clear, crisp, large, and surprisingly unobtrusive.

The EVF also allows a lot of changes in camera settings to be done without removing the camera from your eye. Use the two dials, and you can see where the focus points that you are using are. Hit the OK button on the back, and you can use the dials to adjust just about every setting while watching the selections you are making in the EVF. Ditto with the other buttons like HDR and auto exposure mode.

HDR:
I had the opportunity to use in-camera HDR while on a recent trip. The day was cloudy, and there was a lot of shadow against bright grey clouds. The in-camera HDR used a series of shots at different exposures and combined them in the camera. The results were better than HDR Pro in Photoshop CS5.5 IMO. I was much, much happier with the dynamic range and overall look of the images. the 10 fps shooting mode was also great for minimizing camera movement, ghosts and other problems associated with HDR.

Image stabilization:
The EM-1 has a five axis image stabilization system for the sensor. That means any lens becomes can be used. The fourth and fifth axes are for rotations. One compensates for the slight turn of the camera that often occurs when you press the shutter button. I had good success using IS in low light with my 70-300 mm lens set at 300 mm.

Scenes:
the EM-1 has many useful scene modes. I used landscape and panorama with great success. The artistic filters and story modes may also interest you. I prefer to do those types of things in post-processing.

ISO:
The camera has an almost insane 25600 maximum ISO. Yes, you get image quality degradation and noise at that ISO, but the in-camera JPEG processor can actually give you some relief from the problems at higher ISOs. I so far have found shooting up to ISO 1600 produces no discerned degradation. I tried ISO 6400 and found minimal issues.

For those who started with film and were in love with the "high ISO" 1000 film for low light shooting, this is a major and welcome advancement. For those newer to photography that have been using higher ISO cameras for a while, the speed may not be much of a gain, but the image quality should be.

The low end ISO is 200, which is the new normal. I do not find it to be a problem. I would rather shoot at a faster shutter speed than have an ISO 100 setting in most cases. There is an ISO LOW setting, but I do not plan to use it. If you regularly shoot in bright light and want lower f-stops, invest in a neutral density filter.

Back display:
The back display is slightly disappointing. It can only tilt up and down, not rotate so that you can see your composition when you are getting into the shot. It works well for shooting over crowds or getting a low angle shot.

On the plus side, the display is clear, bright and a touchscreen that can be used to select a point of interest for focusing and can be used to take the shot in live view mode. You can also use it to select settings to change. The next generation should be even better, and hopefully it will have a screen that rotates.

SD card:
One change from the E-500 that I do not like is the use of SD rather than CF cards. CF cards are nearly indestructible, and a good Sansdisk Extreme card works virtually anywhere, anytime and is virtually impossible to physically break. The xD card slot disappearing is no loss, but not having a second card slot is somewhat surprising given the high-end prosumer/professional positioning of this camera.

Controls and customization:
The controls are pretty well placed for me with the exception of the auto exposure lock button. That is right beside the viewfinder and too far to the left for my liking. You can do a lot of customization with the control buttons and dials, but there are limits. I have not made any changes yet because I am still learning the camera. Overall the defaults seem logical and useful.

This camera has two dials, one on the front and one on the back. The E-500 only had a back dial, so I am learning to use the two dial system. They work well for adjusting and selecting options. I think the second dial was a good addition. Both are conveniently located for my fingers.

Image quality:
All of this is meaningless if the image you get out is bad. The EM-1 does not disappoint. I know that there are people who insist that they need 48 MP or some other ridiculously large number. The reality is that 16 MP is a great size for printing full-size 300 dpi images on your printer or using a commercial photo printing service. If all you do is screen displays, it is about eight times more pixels than you need for a typical 2 MP monitor.

The quality of the EM-1 pixels is very high, and you get excellent out-of-the-camera RAW and JPEG images. I have no problems seeing fine detail at 100% and higher magnifications.

Summary:
This camera is a winner, and it works with my existing Four Thirds lenses so I do not have to invest another $3000+ in lenses to use it. I have a lot to learn, and it will take some time to get the most out of the camera, but out-of-the-box, using my E-500 techniques, it is already doing great work.
text_fidelity_b: Olympus OM-D E-M1 16MP Mirrorless Digital Camera with 3-Inch LCD (Body Only) (Silver w/ Black Trim)

ecobee SmartCamera – Indoor WiFi Security Camera, Smart Home Security System, 1080p HD 180 Degree FOV, Night Vision, 2-Way Audio, Works with Apple HomeKit, Alexa Built In Ok, I have to admit I'm pretty impressed with this little camera. At first I thought I had to use the Haven subscription, especially after reading the reviews here which said it is necessary. I was kind of bummed about that at first but it turns out this is really useful even without! Sure, being able to record videos and store them in the cloud require a subscription as well as many of the advanced features, but you can still "arm" the camera to snap a photo and alert your phone when it detects motion, which it does splendidly even without a sub. The way I currently use it, it alerts my phone and I can then go to the live view and see and even interact with who is there (talk feature is really cool!).
On top of that, I set ours up with Amazon's Alexa voice service and it is EXTREMELY COOL! I think the speaker seems a bit louder than an Echo Dot, which surprised me. I'm mounting ours by the front porch so we can see people come to the door and interact with them, but we can also use it to play music via Amazon's Alexa when just sitting on the porch drinking coffee. That's an amazing perk that I wasn't expecting before we got it!
I do wish you could combine it with device music groups in Alexa (so I could say, for example, play this song on the everywhere group and it will play inside on our Echo and out on the porch with the Ecobee), but sadly only echo devices can be grouped. That's OK, I knew that before getting this as other devices in our home can't be grouped either (Facebook Portal or Kindles, for example).
If you want to spring for the subscription service, there's a TON of goodies and advanced features beyond even the cloud storage things. But even without that, the live view and photo motion alerts combined with the voice assistant / Alexa integration makes it worth it even just for the hardware alone!
text_fidelity_b: ecobee SmartCamera – Indoor WiFi Security Camera, Smart Home Security System, 1080p HD 180 Degree FOV, Night Vision, 2-Way Audio, Works with Apple HomeKit, Alexa Built In

text_fidelity_a:
Outdoor WiFi Security Camera, HD 1080P Wireless Survenience IP Camera with 32GB SD Card, IP66 Waterproof Bullet Camera for Home, Support Motion Detection FTP 65ft Night Vision Remote View Onvif Cam [[VIDEOID:bcc01f35bd32d1e66d3df81c3dace063]] Updated as promised: After working with the company I was able to completely secure the camera and still access it remotely. After all the initial problems and concerns I have had it installed and working for about a month I guess. It's working great on a variety of different software and protocols. I even tried connecting it to the Angelcam website and using DDNS. Works great with just about everything. With the 128GB SD card it does great. I uploaded some new photos of it working and the different clients being used securely. This turned out to be a great buy because the image quality is incredible and it's got an incredibly wide angle.

You cannot see the IR light like that at night it's only because of the camera I used you can see it. I did that for a reason so that everyone could see the amount of IR light it puts out. The infrared works great as you can see but the motion sensor even on the least sensitive setting picks up rains and bugs flying in front of it. Almost all motion sensors do. The audio sensor works great but the alarm feature doesn't because it's only one way audio. The email was easy to setup once you know which smtp server your ISP uses which WOW doesn't like giving theirs out even to paying customers. The video was provided by them and helped a lot because the screws were impossible to see and there are unnecessary ones in there that don't need to be removed. I have posted the material they sent me as well. I hope this helps everyone out.

BEFORE EDIT AND CUSTOMER SUPPORT:
So far I have had a lot of issues with this camera and still haven't got it to where I would trust letting it outside my isolated LAN which mean I cannot view remotely as of yet. I changed the 32Gb SD card out to a 128Gb card after contacting support since there is no instructions online or anywhere else on how to do it. Turns out it's the one tiny screw in on the top to remove the black piece and then you must carefully unscrew the lens cap. After that you will find several screws lowered besides the lens and IR area. You only need to remove the 4 of the screws. If you look really close with magnification you can see exactly what screws you need to remove because you can see how they hold the board underneath in place. Underneath the lens is the board that holds the SD-Card. Their support was nice enough to send me a video later on. I plan on posting that later after I get this all working. As of now it is telling me I need to reset the camera and there is no reset button that I can find. I am guessing it must be on that board again which means I am going to have to pull the whole thing apart again. In my opinion this is very poorly designed and not very good for people who like to customize or configure their devices. I do not like the way the it acts as soon as it connects to your network. I am still working on testing and hope I can get these issues resolved soon. The picture quality is great but there is a serious lack of security and other major issues plaguing this device. I am going to do some further testing and contact support once again about resetting this camera hopefully without having to dissemble it again but I don't see how. It has been disconnected for hours without power and will not reset that way. I also notice that the camera unit get's extremely hot for some reason. This will defiantly shorten it's life span. More to come on this product but for now I do not recommend buying this unless you are familiar with IP camera installation, network configuration, and have some electrical experience as far as handling circuit boards. This has been a real pain in the read since day one but I am hoping it will be worth it but time will tell. I will upload the video provided by them after getting their consent.
text_fidelity_b: Outdoor WiFi Security Camera, HD 1080P Wireless Survenience IP Camera with 32GB SD Card, IP66 Waterproof Bullet Camera for Home, Support Motion Detection FTP 65ft Night Vision Remote View Onvif Cam

Zink Polaroid Snap Instant Digital Camera (Pink) with ZINK Zero Ink Printing Technology [[VIDEOID:fab011cbaf4d8ff273fb360a6d075448]] My granddaughter is too young to remember the big bulky Polaroid instant camera, so when I showed her this camera and told her it took instant pictures that she could use as stickers her comment was "AWESOME", and she's dying to get her hands on it. This compact sized 10 megapixel camera offers users the option of printing 2" x 3" photos instantly or adding up to a 32 GB micro SD card in order to store or share images.

The camera is straight forward and simple to use. If you want to take instant photos just load [[ASIN:B00ZSPI3A6 Polaroid 2x3 inch Premium ZINK Photo Paper TWIN PACK (20 Sheets) - Compatible With Polaroid Snap, Z2300, SocialMatic Instant Cameras & Zip Instant Printer]] into the chamber in the back of the camera, remove the magnetic lens cap, and gently press the viewfinder to turn the camera on.

Using the selector wheel at the top left, you can choose to take your photos in color, black & white, or sepia (which is like old time tin type for an antique look). Choose one, and then press the button next to that to select whether you want the photo to have a border or not. You can even press another button on the top to activate a 10 second delay to take selfies, and there's also a "photo booth mode" which takes a series of six quick pictures over the course of 10 seconds that you can set by depressing the shutter for three seconds.

Once you've chosen all of your desired options simply frame your shot in the viewfinder and press the shutter. There's no zoom or available adjustment, the camera automatically focuses and uses flash if needed, and the 2" x 3" print comes out of the side of the camera clear, sharp, and dry to the touch in under a minute. If you have film loaded the camera is going to print photos automatically when you press the shutter, so don't load paper if you prefer to use the micro SD card and not print. The camera has an auto sleep function that will shut it off to save battery power if sufficient times lapses between use, or you can just press the viewfinder back down to shut it off manually.

There are no instructions that comes with the camera, but you can read or print the manual yourself by going to polaroidsnapcamera dot come. You can also find the firmware update there. Be sure to charge the camera fully when you receive it, then insert a Micro SD card and update the firmware before using it. (Available here: http://polaroid.com/products/polaroid-snap-camera) Besides printing paper, you'll definitely want to have a MicroSD card for the camera and a case: [[ASIN:B017A1D6TI Polaroid Neoprene Pouch for The Polaroid Snap Instant Camera (Black)]].

There are several things about this product that could be improved on:
1. No sample printing paper included
2. No picture preview
3. No strap to attach the lens cover to which would help prevent losing it
4. Viewfinder pops open too easily
5. No instruction manual or link mention of the firmware update (or link to it) included with product

Otherwise, the camera is well made and fun to use. I can see where kids would have a lot of fun with this camera, but the photo paper isn't cheap so I may let my granddaughter use some and then just mostly use the Micro SD card. This could also be useful for producing instant photos at special events such as birthday parties, weddings, proms, and for other occasions, and the peel off backing on the photo paper makes it nice for scrap booking.

This instant camera was provided at no cost for my evaluation and review.
text_fidelity_b: Zink Polaroid Snap Instant Digital Camera (Pink) with ZINK Zero Ink Printing Technology

Echo Glow - Multicolor smart lamp, a Certified for Humans Device – Requires compatible Alexa device I am not the target demographic for this device: middle-aged empty nester who loves to watch sci-fi, thrillers, and horror. I have a number of these brilliantly simple, highly configurable lights. They are perfect in the bedroom where, depending on our intended mood, a variety of different colors or modes might be appropriate. I have two in the living room, hiding behind tropical plants at a 3' height, on either side of the big screen, about 5 feet away on each side. I have a routine set up to turn off all the lights in the room and engage campfire mode in both lights at 45% brightness with a single keyword. Voila--instant torchlight in the jungle (or romantic candlelight - take your pick). I am a colossal LOST fan, and this lighting is perfect for watching LOST, or anything scary or dark. And if I need a different effect, that's only a few words away.

The simplicity with which these set up and configure themselves is so good it makes Apple products jealous. If you have an Alexa on your Wi-Fi network, simply plug the Glow in to a power source, open the Alexa app on your phone, and the light will auto-connect to your network and add itself to Alexa. It will then prompt you to configure it with a name and add it to any groups, etc. Utterly simple. If the setup fails, it might ask you to scan the barcode on the back of the booklet it came with to get it going, but this has not been my experience - they have all self-configured and join the network seamlessly.

For those of you complaining this does not have a mic and speaker - folks, it works WITH an Echo device. It is a light - that's it. If Amazon built Alexa mics and speakers into this it would cost double--and I am positive they are developing just such a light ...for which you will pay $60+.

Normally, these are $30/ea, but they were 45% off on Prime Day, so I added a few more. There are indeed cheaper (and much more expensive) smart mood lights on the market, but if you run Alexa at home, this is hands down the best way to do it. Seamless.

It baffles me that Amazon does not have a whole range of lighting products which work exactly like this. They easily could. Give me one of these on a larger scale (12-15") and make it weatherproof for outside on the patio, please.
text_fidelity_b: Echo Glow - Multicolor smart lamp, a Certified for Humans Device – Requires compatible Alexa device

text_fidelity_a:
iPad Stand TechMatte Multi-Angle Aluminum Holder for Tablets, E-Readers and Smartphones, Nintendo Switch - Mini Stand The heft of this stand is impressive. I was expecting a lightweight stand, but was really surprised at how heavy and solid it was when I took it out of the box. It's the type of stand that I get the impression that I could run over with my car and not damage it. The hinge and the "kick stand" portion are made of plastic, but they also feel substantial.

The angle is set by depressing a button in the hinge area. It's very easy to adjust, and the hinge has click stops at various angles that hold it securely.

What is not adjustable is the depth of the cutout that holds the tablet or phone. I didn't have any problems with it holding a variety of tablets (iPad, Kindle and Nexus). It won't, however, hold some tablets that have a skin on it. The cutout that holds the table is slanted, and is 10mm at the widest point at the top, and 8mm at the narrowest point at the bottom. You'll want to measure your tablet plus skin to make sure it fits.

The cutout for the tablet has a plastic non-skid insert that works well. The stand itself also has plastic nubs on the back to prevent scratches on the tablet, and nubs on the bottom to prevent scratches on the table top. The nubs also act as non-skid points.

Very solid build quality, very easy to adjust in a variety of angles, and the design ensures that there won't be any damage to the tablet when you take if off/put it on the stand. As long as the width does not present a problem, this is a great choice for a tablet stand. Highly recommend.
[Sample provided for review]
text_fidelity_b: iPad Stand TechMatte Multi-Angle Aluminum Holder for Tablets, E-Readers and Smartphones, Nintendo Switch - Mini Stand

As can be seen, the video is grainy (even at highest resolution), unclear, and the voice is not great even though the camera was right next to my mouth.

I also tested this camera with my video reviews. If the camera is no more than 12 inches from the object or my voice, it takes okay video but any movement turns into a blur. When shooting video from about two feet away, it is almost a complete blur with the voice barely being heard and I was using a tripod.

This camera comes with two re-chargeable batteries, a 16GB SD card, a USB cable with AC adapter, absolutely lousy instructions, cables for connecting camera to TV, and a thumb drive with two slots for the SD card. It also comes with a case.

The camera has to be charged for at least six hours before use. It is somewhat easy to figure out using the display and menu buttons but it would have been great to have good instructions. The display playback appears to be frame by frame and not full video replay--at least I could not get full video replay. There is a wide angle and telephoto button. The camera is easy to hold and record with and there is a tripod hole. However, I absolutely hate the results and am sorry I ordered this due the substandard quality of the video it produces.

Kindle Oasis E-reader (Previous Generation - 9th) - Graphite, 7" High-Resolution Display (300 ppi), Waterproof, Built-In Audible, 8 GB, Wi-Fi - Includes Special Offers (Closeout) Some people have claimed the screen is square, it's not. Like all previous Kindles this is measured diagonally. It only appears square because the one side of the bezel with the buttons (also not loud as has been claimed and the touch screen works fine if the nearly inaudible click might keep a partner awake).
I really like the seven inch screen and design of this new Kindle it's much closer to a regular paperback page now. I do wish the boldness option was allowed to be applied to any book and not just those purchased from Amazon. I get plenty of books from other sites such as Baen and Project Gutenberg but they're not given the full functionality Amazon's books are. I don't think it's fair.
The weight and balance. In or out of the cover is almost perfect. I find I can comfortably read for hours and if either hand gets tired a quick flip and you're reading with the other. I've reversed the page turn buttons like on the old K3/Kindle keyboard the page forward button is more natural feeling if it's at the bottom I have no idea why Amazon has the default reversed. Holding it you're more apt to go forward than bsck plus if you need to go back you can just slide your finger towards the screen and use the touch screen to go back, then it's right back to the lower button to continue reading. I rather like this device. It's noy light years ahead of the Voyage or PaperWhite but it is certainly a few large steps ahead. I haven't and have no plans to test the waterproof claims. I like the idea because I'm disabled and on a walker my previous Kindles have gotten damp. Now i don't have to worry. I did pour a few drops of water on the cover. All but one rolled off. The one soaked in. Caveat emptor. Im happy with the purchase so far. It was a gift to myself for having quit smoking for 10 full years. I deserved it.
text_fidelity_b: Kindle Oasis E-reader (Previous Generation - 9th) - Graphite, 7" High-Resolution Display (300 ppi), Waterproof, Built-In Audible, 8 GB, Wi-Fi - Includes Special Offers (Closeout)

text_fidelity_a:
Harman Kardon Allure Voice-Activated Home Speaker with Alexa, Black As an avid fan of Alexa, I am delighted to have this Harman Kardon Alexa speaker. I've had my original Echo since the first week they released the initial invitation to buy and have since added a Dot and Alexa controlled thermostats, dining room lights, Fire TV sticks and plugs through out the house. This unit was meant to enhance the music sound quality from Alexa and expand our Alexa listening group and work with the living room television.

The speaker itself is considerably larger than my original Echo - wider and heavier. The lights on this are brighter as well - when playing music at night or listening to a book, you can leave the light on and it works as a night light. You can also turn the light off if you prefer. Setting this up takes a bit longer than my Echo or Dot - it's slower making the initial WiFi connection, but once you link to Amazon via the Alexa App, you're good to go. It connects via Bluetooth to both my LG V10 phone and my Samsung tablets without drama.

This unit is significantly louder at every volume setting than the original Echo and makes the Dot sound like she's whispering. I have this in our formal living room where we have 30 feet tall ceilings, grass cloth covered walls and an enormous open space - the room was designed for correct accoustics with my Grandmother's grand piano and music simply sounds beautiful in here. The Harman Kardon Alexa sits on a table where the piano used to be and the sound at volume 4 simply envelopes you no matter where you are in the room. Set the volume to 6 and I can hear my book or music two rooms away almost as if it's floating through the halls. The sound quality is excellent and playing Beethoven or opera or country music renders each instrument precisely from tiny flutes to cellos and twangy fiddles. I'm immensely pleased at the improvement from the Echo to this for just music.

The reason for the one star deduction is because I thought/expected the Harman Kardon to by fully, 100% integrated with Alexa. It is not. This unit cannot be linked to the Fire TV sticks, meaning that I cannot use it to verbally control the living room television. It cannot be linked to my Echo and Dot units. That means we can't include the Harman Kardon speaker in our multi room group so the same song/book can be heard throughout the house. We cannot do the Drop In skill where Alexa acts as an intercom system for multiple rooms. There are a couple of other skills this speaker isn't able to perform simply because it doesn't speak to the Amazon Alexa products. If they can correct this glaring deficiency, then this would be a five star product and one i would consider buying for the guest suite and master bedroom. As a stand alone Alexa unit, this is a top notch choice, but if you want to link to your existing Echo, you can't do so.
text_fidelity_b: Harman Kardon Allure Voice-Activated Home Speaker with Alexa, Black

I shopped at a variety of stores. I was surprised to find that some of the companies known for sturdy cell phone cases did not offer the same quality to fit tablets. Notably absent was protection for the corners.
My search finally paid off as the ZUGU case is ideal. it is sturdy without excessive bulk. It protects all sides of the tablet including the corners. Given the snug fit, I found it initially a challenge to attach the ZUGU case. . This is before I found the best approach was to slip the top right hand corner of the case last over the tablet frame. Due to the openings, the case material was s thinner and more flexible here. But do be careful not to pull too hard: The corner should slip readily over the frame here if the remaining sides are snug.
Another unique feature is that the company may offer to cover the copay if the owner has Apple Care and the screen breaks. (Please check the manufacturer website for detail).I
There is one trade.off with the case: it is purely functional rather than being a fashion statement. But I personally prefer protection to good looks and will enclose it with some confidence in a tote.

Bluetooth Headphones Wireless Earbuds Sports Over-Ear Bluetooth 5.3 Ear Buds with Earhooks 120H Playtime Wireless Headphones for Workout Waterproof Audifonos Bluetooth inalambricos LED Power Display I find that the best price to performance is in the $30 range for Bluetooth headphones, and they keep getting better and better. I have several pairs that I use for the gym, general listening to music, watching movies, and playing poker. I like to have other charged ones ready to go if a pair gets low.

These were rated very well, so I decided to give them a shot. They are super comfortable and they stay in place at the gym. I am not an audiophile, but these are well balanced and have better sound quality than my other pairs.

The greatest thing about these is the battery life- I used them for about 11 hours, and there was still 50% battery life left. With all my other pairs the battery life is a real problem, and it does not improve as they age. The charging case is also nice and there is a display for remaining battery life of the case. Remaining battery life of the headphones is displayed on the mobile device.

The BT connection is also super reliable. I have not experienced any disconnects or interference.

There are a couple cons (no product is perfect) and I want to briefly discuss them.

1. The rubber snap-on ear buds are not universal. They have a unique oval shape where they snap on and are secured. I have a bunch of spares, but they will not fit on here. If you lose one or it breaks it is useless. It comes with 3 sizes, but most people are probably like me and can only use the one size that fits.

2. The gain is too high on these. Adjusting the volume from zero, there are not many steps until the volume is too high. This means that micro-adjustment of the volume is not possible. All my other pairs I can use at 100% volume or near this (though I would not recommend it) and there there are maybe 15 or more micro-adjustments all the way back down to zero. Also, the notifications "power on," "power off," and "connected" are too loud. It's possible that with different mobile phones they behave differently, and there may also be an adjustment for this.

In summary, I highly recommend these. They are comfortable, they stay in place, they stay connected to my device, and they sound great. Probably the biggest Pro is the battery life. I purchased these to use as a backup for my other pairs, but it turns out that these will be my main headphones.
text_fidelity_b: Bluetooth Headphones Wireless Earbuds Sports Over-Ear Bluetooth 5.3 Ear Buds with Earhooks 120H Playtime Wireless Headphones for Workout Waterproof Audifonos Bluetooth inalambricos LED Power Display

text_fidelity_a:
FULLJA WiFi Digital Picture Frame - 10.1 Inch Smart Digital Photo Frame with FHD IPS Touch Screen, 32GB Memory, Motion Sensor WiFi Electronic Picture Frame Share Photos and Videos Via App Email I don’t love it. This seems overpriced for what you get. For the price, I was expecting it to look more like a photo frame but instead, it kinda feels like an old monitor. My goal was to hang it on the wall during art shows with process videos playing. It will work OK for that but I’m disappointed that unless the video is in the exact proportion of the frame, it will always look a little “off” and there’s no means of changing how it’s framed in the display.

I think it’s at its best without the clock or any other additions.

The pros: It really does work right out of the box. It only took minutes to get photos onto it. The big screen is nice, I can see details in my photos. It is also bright with vivid colors. I like that it is flat which is why it performs better than an average monitor as a picture frame. The simple black frame doesn’t detract from its appearance. I like that there is an app and my husband and I were able to add photos, and I also like that there is a way to add photos via card in case software changes make the app obsolete. With the app, I was able to get videos onto it in minutes. I also like that it has a large amount of storage space and the means to expand it..

The cons: It is slow. I didn’t love the way the photos are displayed. I also hate the default animations because they are a bit cheesy. I want it to fade or some other non-intrusive way to change photos, and there is no means to edit it. The features are incredibly barebones. I hate that the default includes the time etc, I just want it to look like a photo frame! The audio is a bit tinny, much more so than a television etc. I also find it bizarre in 2023 to have an item that warns that it can destroy a USB if it’s removed without turning it off first…that seems like such an old-school problem!

I wish the plug was white because the black looks bad against the wall, and I prefer a minimalist look.

For the price, I feel like this could be better. There are just so few options for customizing the display.
text_fidelity_b: FULLJA WiFi Digital Picture Frame - 10.1 Inch Smart Digital Photo Frame with FHD IPS Touch Screen, 32GB Memory, Motion Sensor WiFi Electronic Picture Frame Share Photos and Videos Via App Email

HDD/SDD management is really neat--it's behind the motherboard instead of at the front base of the case, saving precious room for large GPUs if that is your thing. I really like how the case is the size of a mATX case, but it can comfortably fit a standard ATX motherboard due to the ability to change where the PSU goes.

At this moment, I cannot speak for how cool the case keeps yet, but the whole thing is essentially a grate, so I can't imagine the air flow being bad. I suggested he get a few more fans just to keep air flowing through the filters, as they impede flow a fair amount, just like all the non-foam filters I've dealt with. If need be, the filters can be easily removed to allow the system to cool more effectively.

If I need to get a new case for some reason, I will probably get this.

text_fidelity_a:
Sony ICF-506 Analog Tuning Portable FM/AM Radio, Black, 2.14 lb Growing up I always had a radio in my room. Times are a little different now and I tend to get my music from the Internet, but there are still times when local radio stations are a better choice - particularly during power outages or when getting local news. I have had very good fortune with Sony electronics and computers in the past so I was eager to try this AM/FM tuner and had high expectations. It did not disappoint me.

Let me very clear about this unit - it is for AM/FM receiving only. It does not play MP3’s, it doesn’t play CDs and it doesn’t stream from the Internet. It’s just an AM/FM tuner. It does this quite well, though - better than most other tuners I have used in the last several years.

Right out of the box, this unit looks nostalgic. It has a classic AM/FM radio look and feel, very similar to a radio my father used to have in his workshop when I was a kid. This is a big plus for me, just for the fact that it takes me back to my childhood.

I plugged it in and turned it on, and I immediately tuned to one of the [relatively] local stations. It picked it up and played it very clearly, better than most other tuners I have used in the last 4-5 years. It is definitely better than the car’s radio. I “surfed” the dial and found other stations that I have listened to in the past but thought were out of range and this little radio did a good job of picking them up and playing with minimal static. That’s really all I could ask. It’s not a miracle radio though and it cannot pick up FM stations hundreds of miles away, but it has better range than most I have used recently.

I like that it can be used on AC power or on batteries. That will be handy during weather events.

I can’t find any real reason to complain about this tuner. It works great and looks great too. It is a little on the pricey side which is par for the course for Sony electronics, but it is a fine tuner that is worth its asking price.
text_fidelity_b: Sony ICF-506 Analog Tuning Portable FM/AM Radio, Black, 2.14 lb

I own about a dozen radios that cost around $400 each. They are incredibly high quality and obviously very expensive too. But they are not the kind of radios you would camp or backpack with. They are too heavy and large for that application.

So, I did my research and bought these Midland radios. AND THEY ARE GREAT!! They have a clear and strong signal under reasonable conditions for ANY radio. Radios--whether they are $400 each or $40 each, cannot overcome solid obstacles like houses and trees and mountains indefinitely. I was impressed at how well these did under less than ideal conditions.

Ignore these reviewers that have unattainable standards and get these radios.

text_fidelity_a: Bluetooth Audio Adapter for Music Streaming Sound System, esinkin W29-us Wireless Audio Adapter Works with Smart Phones and Tablets, Wireless Adapter for Speakers OK, it's easy to use and works great!  Now, the rest of the story:  When you use it, it identifies itself as headphones.  Seems ok, but then you leave the house with your phone and you will miss every call and audible notation because it thinks it is still connected to headphones.  The solution is simple -- you must go into your phone settings and select bluetooth>Esinkin BT Adapter>Forget this Device.  That's right, every time you want to use it you have to pair it and then Forget it when done.  Simply "disconnecting" it only lasts a few seconds and your phone returns to headphone mode.  Now, if I am all wrong about this, please correct me and let everyone else know.  This would be great for a retired phone you use as your music box and stays connected to your sound system all the time.  But for an active phone, it's a PIA.

As this one had threads that weren't smooth about halfway down on the screw/bolt, it left the screw/bolt jutted out. The base won't sit on the nightstand or other flat surface with this issue unless he just doesn't use the screw/bolt. I'd post a photo for clarification but the stand isn't available and getting him to send photos isn't always something I remember when we do talk.

The screw/bolt is I'm sure metric and it does use an Allen wrench (included) to screw in; the threading is very tight, so finding a true replacement screw/bolt is probably gonna require going to a specialty nuts/bolts/hardware store. That's annoying enough to take off 1.5 stars for me.

Zink Polaroid Snap Instant Digital Camera (Pink) with ZINK Zero Ink Printing Technology I grew up loving my Polaroid instant prints. This modern version not only gives you the instant gratification of a print (that we all know and love), but it also peels off and actually doubles as a STICKER! How cool is that! Teenage-me would have loved having one of these instead of taping stuff to the wall.

If instant gratification is your thing or you just have a nostalgia for old Polaroid concepts, this camera is for you!

text_fidelity_a:
Fujifilm Instax Mini 26 + Rainbow Film Bundle - Black A long time ago I had access to a Polaroid Instamatic camera. It was great - snap a picture, it spits out a sheet. Wait about 2 minutes and what you have is a printed photograph. Polaroid is gone now (though the name gets licensed over and over again), and with it went all of the film for the camera that made it so useful. This new camera by Fuji brings back some of the fun of instant photos, though it is by no means perfect and it suffers from some of the same issues the older Polaroid camera had.

The idea is very straightforward - point-and-shoot, and the camera ejects an exposure that will develop over a few moments and will be fully developed in approximately 2 minutes. This is great for social events and is a fun way to share candid shots. The camera is very lightweight and it is small too so it is easy to pack and carry with you.

There are a few issues with the camera, though, some of which are very much like the old Polaroids of days gone by. The images do come out a bit grainy and are definitely not high resolution. If you are looking for images with nice, clean edge detail and bright, vibrant colors, this is going to disappoint you. Also, the images are really small, a little bigger than a passport picture but not by very much. And finally, the film is relatively expensive, a pack of exposures coming with only 10 slides and costing about $0.60 per exposure.

On the plus side, the camera is very easy to use and the camera body itself is not very expensive at all.

There are trade-offs with this camera. On one hand, it is super convenient, it’s fun and it’s relatively inexpensive. However, exposure quality is mediocre, pictures are small and on a per-picture basis the exposures are somewhat expensive. To me, the fun factor weighs heavily in favor of this camera and offsets some of the negatives. For social gatherings and recreational events, this is a fun camera and will serve well. Do not expect to have high-end results, though.
text_fidelity_b: Fujifilm Instax Mini 26 + Rainbow Film Bundle - Black

Logitech Harmony 950 Touch IR Remote Control - Discontinued by Manufacturer Logitech makes the best universal remote controls and they keep introducing new models that are better and better. If you have half a dozen (or more) remote controls on your living room table and are always losing some of them or forgetting which does what, then a universal remote is for you.

The Harmony 950 appears to be mostly the same as the Harmony Elite, except without the Harmony Hub device. The Harmony Hub can be purchased separately later, though the Elite package is cheaper if you're getting it anyway. The Harmony Hub greatly expands the range and capabilities of your Harmony remote, so you should think twice before skipping it.

Logitech also sells much cheaper Harmony remotes without the touch screen. The main benefit of the touch screen is to program shortcuts to your favorite TV channels and to control more devices than the non-touch remote controls can access. If you always use your DVR or cable box's on-screen channel menu and only have a few devices, then maybe a much cheaper Harmony without the touch screen is a better value for you.

The Harmony is pretty easy to program by connecting to your PC and connecting to the Logitech website. If you have an older Harmony remote, you may be able to transfer all your device settings to this one. The buttons on the Harmony are easy to see, well spaced and give you good feedback when pressed.

Battery life is OK for a touchscreen device, but like your smartphone you will need to recharge this at least every couple of days. Most people will leave the Harmony in the recharging station most of the time, so make sure you have an electrical outlet close to where you will be using the Harmony.

If you're in the market for a universal remote, Logitech Harmony should be first on your list. The only decision you have to make is which model to buy. If you're trying to control a handful of devices (TV, cable box, DVR, stereo system, game system, DVD player), then you really have to ask yourself if the touchscreen feature is worth the big price premium. If you have a "smart home" with remote controlled lights, outlets, thermostat, etc or if your devices are spread around a large room so the IR remote has trouble connecting with them, then the Harmony Hub is a good idea.
text_fidelity_b: Logitech Harmony 950 Touch IR Remote Control - Discontinued by Manufacturer

You can indeed connect the soundbar to an Echo device *as a regular bluetooth connection*, but the instructions to enable Auto VA (auto virtual assistant mode) via Bluetooth so the soundbar maintains a BT connection with Echo while using other inputs DOESN'T WORK. The instructions say to first connect the soundbar to Echo via BT (✅), and then to press the Bluetooth button for 10 seconds to enable Auto VA (❌). HOWEVER; after five seconds, the soundbar enters Bluetooth pairing mode. I've tried dozens of times, connecting and disconnecting the BT connection with Echo and restarting and resetting the soundbar: NO DICE.

It's frustrating because this feature is in the title of the product and is clearly described in the User Manual — and yet it doesn't work at all.

I imagine Auto VA via AUX input works okay, but that means I have to move my Echo or get a wicked-long audio cable, neither of which I want to do.

However, otherwise the soundbar sounds fine. Not quite as good as the Bose Companion computer speakers I used previously, but whole worlds better than the built in TV speakers. It's just a shame that I have disconnect and reconnect to Alexa so often.

text_fidelity_a: GEEKOM Mini AIR11 Mini PC Windows 11, 8GB RAM Dual DDR4 256GB M.2 SSD, Mini NUC Computer with Intel 11th Gen N5095, Home/Business Mini Desktop Computer, 4K UHD/Dual WiFi/BT4.2/HDMI/Gigabit Ethernet It amazes me just how much power this little computer has.  It runs silently and generates almost no heat.  So far I have only used it with Wi-Fi and the performance has been quite good.  I want to try it with an ethernet cable, directly connected to see if performance is even better.  The biggest struggle that I had in dealing with this computer is that it has Windows 11 installed.  Not being familiar with 11, since all my other PCs have Win 10, I had a hard time finding some commonly used functions.  Of course that is not the fault of the computer.  There are some things to be aware of if you buy this.  First of all, you need a monitor, keyboard and mouse to use with the computer, since it doesn't come with these items.  Secondly, the computer seems to use all the latest connection types, such as HDMI for video.  All but one of my monitors don't have HDMI, but only DVI and/or VGA connectors.  If you don't have an HDMI connection on your monitor, you will need an adapter or adapter cable that converts the type of connector that you have to HDMI.  There is an included HDMI cable, with both ends HDMI.  There also is a mini display port connector, which I am not familiar with.  The mouse and keyboard could be another issue.  All my mice use the round PS/2 type connectors and some of my available keyboards are the same way with the old PS/2 connector.  To connect to the Geekom, you either need a USB keyboard and mouse (which will use up 2 of the 3 available USB ports) or your need a wireless keyboard and mouse.  Wireless may use one or two USB ports, depending on whether the receiver for the mouse and keyboard is integrated to handle both or if you have a keyboard and a mouse from different manufacturers, which requires two receivers, instead of one.  A good feature this computer has is a mounting bracket that allows you to mount it to the back of certain monitors, which is a space saver.  You really don't need this, as the computer is so small anyway that the footprint is minimal.  The only thing I would have liked on this is a DVI connector.  Also, the manual is very minimal.  Currently the computer goes to sleep after a few minutes and I have to press the power button to get it to wake up.  This could be normal behavior and I have an inquiry in to Geekom to find out.  I love this little computer and I will probably never buy a full sized computer again.  Storage is limited, but I keep all my data on external network drives and backed up to the cloud, so a lot of storage on the computer is not an issue these days.  If you can deal with the newer connection types with this computer, I think you will really love it.  I am really happy with it.  It is hard to find anything wrong with this computer.  I think it seems to be quite sturdy too, as the UPS delivery man just dropped the package with a big thump by my front door.  I was afraid it might damage the computer, but it worked fine, so I guess it can handle some bumps and thumps, as it was not packed with a lot of cushioning material.
text_fidelity_b: GEEKOM Mini AIR11 Mini PC Windows 11, 8GB RAM Dual DDR4 256GB M.2 SSD, Mini NUC Computer with Intel 11th Gen N5095, Home/Business Mini Desktop Computer, 4K UHD/Dual WiFi/BT4.2/HDMI/Gigabit Ethernet

text_fidelity_a:
Garmin nüvi 360 3.5-Inch Bluetooth Portable GPS Navigator with Text-To-Speech (Discontinued by Manufacturer) I've had this Nuvi 360 since Dec, 2006. It really works well. I carried it with me to DC. Even on foot it was terrific. It knew where all the restaurants and points of interest were and faithfully navigated us around the ancient horse paths of the Virginia/DC area. Believe me, when you pop out of an underground Metro station in the middle of the night and have no idea where you are or which direction to head off in, the ol' Garmin was there.

It's so small it easily fits in a pocket. The built-in battery lasts reasonably long. In the car, the 12-Volt adapter allows the unit to stay on indefinitely. You can select which accent and which gender you want the voice prompts to speak. Australian "Bruce," American "Jill" and a host of other combinations. All very fun. The voice prompts are the best. You really don't need to look at the thing while driving because it's uncanny in telling you what to do when you need to do it. It is amazingly accurate: something like 20 feet. It takes you right to the destination driveway.

It acquires the sats quickly and doesn't get flustered if you violate its recommendation and go in a different route. It just says, "recalculating" and finds another route for you. None of this "make a U-turn, bonehead!" It gives you enough time to make the turns, too. Also, it displays how far it is until the next turn. Very nice. No need to worry if you've missed it.

If you are planning on going to Europe, buy the unit that comes preloaded with both US and Europe maps as purchasing the Europe maps after the fact will really jump the cost unnecessarily.

I haven't used the Bluetooth capability yet but might later...after I get a Bluetooth phone.

The display is quite viewable in daylight and very bright at night, though it can be set to auto-dim at sundown so it's not too bright at night. You can touch the screen and scroll the map under your finger much like Google Maps can, to preview your route if desired. It shows coordinates and you can save them as destinations if desired, even if the location doesn't have an official street address. It is an MP3 player and can display photos and play Audible books on tape. When you are using the MP3 or Audible features, it pauses the file playing back to announce directions, then returns to the file without losing any of the MP3 file or book info. Very nice.

At extra cost, it has the ability to add foreign language dictionaries which can verbally speak phrases and words to you. You can also add Travel Guides and other software via the SD chip slot.

Overall, I'm very pleased with this device. It's accurate, fast, functional and small.

The one thing that doesn't work is the windshield suction mount. It broke before I even used it once. The plastic loops on the suction cup that receive the ball arm's hinge pin are too thin and fragile and broke with just a little normal hinge adjustment.

I recommend the model 010-10908-00 friction mount that looks like a bean bag with a ball arm sticking up. I made something similar by taking an unneeded 1/4" thick mousepad and epoxying a couple of small 1" x 1" angle brackets to the pad to hold the ball arm that I salvaged from the broken suction cup mount.

A friction mount is interchangeable with multiple vehicles, doesn't slide around on the dash and allows complete and rapid removal and/or hiding to avoid theft. Plus, you don't have to glue a disk to the dash for the suction cup to attach to.

UPDATE 10-22-07:
The 360 works well enough; better than most. It should: Five point three bills should deliver one heck of a map!

I've had it since Dec 2006...less than one year. Today I get an offer from Garmin to update my North American map software for a mere point seven bills. That's AFTER the five point three bills I already sunk into this little electronic gizmo.

I heard Garmin has a one year free map update policy, but their website won't let me do it. Not cool. The cost of the unit has already fallen significantly from what I originally paid and now they want more to get it current, within a year of purchase. Not cool at all. Also, impossible to contact by email. Garmin website is in a permanent loop back to itself when clicking on the "contact by email" option. Otherwise, it's call and wait on hold between certain times. Not cool again.

Then a friend says how well his Verizon GPS works on his wireless phone. I look into that. Verizon offers a full time GPS cost and a single use option for under three bucks per use.

For what I have wasted on this Garmin--over five bills and counting upward forever with their unfriendly updates--that's a whole heck of a lot of one-time Verizon uses with what will be the most updated, most accurate database. After all, no one's going to beat the phone company with accurate phone numbers and addresses.

If I hadn't already bought into the Garmin ripoff, I'd definitely go with Verizon's phone based GPS: the phone will always be with you when you need it instead of in the glove compartment in the other car.

And it most likely won't get stolen. It's a darned pain to have to put the Garmin away after each use so some cretin won't bash in a window to steal a very, very expensive toy that could just as easily fit inside a phone.

Go with the phone.
text_fidelity_b: Garmin nüvi 360 3.5-Inch Bluetooth Portable GPS Navigator with Text-To-Speech (Discontinued by Manufacturer)

Quality of the sound is important for concert and other live music gigs. But those big Sonys take up a lot of space, so I've been considering a good set of IEMs for a while now. In the past I haven't had good results from anything that wasn't a large over-the-ear set, and I have small ears that reject a lot of ear-bud style devices so I was excited to get a chance to try these out.

Ok, to be fair, I don't have any other IEMs to compare this to, but I'm BLOWN AWAY at how incredible they sound at such a miniscule size. I put on the smallest tips for my ears and they actually stay in relatively well, and create the passive noise cancellation I was expecting but without being uncomfortable to wear for an extended period of time. But the range of sound reproduced was something I have only experienced in larger studio headphones!
A perk of IEMs versus larger headphones on jobs like mine are that I can pull out one so I can hear the sound around me while monitoring with my other ear (great if working with an audio engineer who needs to communicate with me on the job), and it comes with a pretty nifty case to wrap it up and slide into my bag. The case makes it bigger than it needs to be, but honestly this is so much less space than my old headphones took up, and keeps the cord from getting tangled. I love it!
For personal use, they sound great even on consumer equipment, but they really shine on devices that can drive the additional range such as my old LG V20 with it's Quad DAC built in (one of the reasons I keep that old device around!).
The price tag is a little steep for me personally, but my Sony headphones retail somewhere around this (I had bought them used), and I KNOW there are pricier options out there, so it seems to fit right into the audiophile equipment range.
text_fidelity_b: Technics Premium in- Ear Monitors IEM, High-Fidelity Wired in-Ear Earbuds Earphones with Innovative 10mm Driver for Ultra-Low Distortion - EAH-TZ700, Black/Gold

All-New Fire HD 8 Screen Protector,Tempered Glass Screen Protector Film for All-New Fire HD 8 Tablet with Alexa (7th 2017 Release) [9H Hardness] [Crystal Clear] [Bubble Free] I've used glass screen protectors on several smartphones and digital cameras. This is my first time trying a large glass screen protector on a tablet. The kit contains everything you need, including a alcohol towel for cleaning your tablet (and your fingers), a sticker that tries to pick up all the lint on the tablet and the screen protector, and various other things that are less necessary. The glass is fine. It is slightly smaller than the Fire 8's screen (so you have some leeway if you don't install it perfectly). There is a little hole at the top so it doesn't cover the selfie camera. Honestly, I haven't noticed much difference between different brands of screen protectors.

If you've never installed a glass screen protector before, look on YouTube for tutorials. All of the similar products are installed the same way. You need to be really careful when installing this thing since it is large and difficult to align with your tablet's screen. I suggest that you try to align one edge of the protector as well as the camera hole and then hope for the best with the other edges. Make sure you pick up all the lint on both the tablet screen and the back of the screen protector, since any stray dust or lint is going to be noticeably ugly for as long as you have the screen protector installed. If you try to remove the screen protector to wipe off some lint that you missed, I guarantee that more lint will sucked in and make the problem worse, so you're best off doing a very thorough cleaning job the first time.

Whether or not you actually need a screen protector is a good question. If you use a case with a cover, then your chance of scratching the screen is small. I guess that depends on how rough you are with your tablet. You can go by your experience with other devices. A tablet is not like a smartphone that is sitting in your pocket with loose change and keys.
text_fidelity_b: All-New Fire HD 8 Screen Protector,Tempered Glass Screen Protector Film for All-New Fire HD 8 Tablet with Alexa (7th 2017 Release) [9H Hardness] [Crystal Clear] [Bubble Free]

Even with that, I still believe this air blower deserves at least 4.5 Stars ✨ and I definitely recommend it.

Cooler Master Hyper 212 EVO V2 CPU Air Cooler with SickleFlow 120, PWM Fan, Direct Contact Technology, 4 Copper Heat Pipes for AMD Ryzen/Intel LGA1700/1200/1151, Silver/Black I have had this CPU fan now going on 5 months. I love this fan. I hadn't upgraded for nearly 10 years and decided on an AMD FM2 Black Edition 6300 6-core CPU with an MSI 970A-G43 Plus economy Micro Board and 16GB of Corsair Memory 4GBx4 in the 4 slots. I use my computer for gaming and all around use. I wanted a CPU cooler that would be quiet and still keep my cpu cool when I cranked it up for high-performance gaming. I found it with this AND it didn't break the bank. With the Turbo Clock OC setting it will idle down and bolt up to 4300mhz seamlessly while the fan moves from it's WHISPER silent 36c idle and general use, to it's 42c full bore o'clocked gaming use. The fan keeps it cool, and never does the fan become obtrusive or loud.

This fan is BIG. Don't even consider it if you have a micro or small mid-tower case. Your case must be generous in it's width to accommodate this cooler. Be sure to check the dimensions of your case with the unit. I have an older Antec 900 case it fit snugly into. I did have to remove the optional side window cooler intake fan I had installed with the prev board, cpu and cooler to allow it's fit. Also be sure your motherboard design placement of Memory slots is such that your Memory will clear it. My board's Corsair Vengence Memory JUST cleared it by a couple mm's laterally, and the top of the memory overtakes the bottom edge of cooler by about a quarter inch. If you are in the process of building your system a choice with low profile memory that doesn't have the tall heat spreaders would be a wise choice and safe bet if you are unsure about clearance with a board design that puts the memory slots very close to the CPU and cooler position. In the first photo attached I REVERSED the fan position to PULL the air thru on Left for best clearance instead of PUSHING the air through on the right if you just don't have the room, that flexibility is very handy. I wasn't satisfied with the cooling level and re-positioned the fan on right to PUSH it through later on and it sent the temps down a few more degrees. As you can see though in the second photo, it is much more snug.

Bottom line, a great cooler IF your case and build offers the room to fit it in. I would recommend it for those wanting great overclocking cooling performance and very quiet operation. I think most overclock enthusiasts would be well served to try this value priced solution before expensive and complicated water cooled solutions.
text_fidelity_b: Cooler Master Hyper 212 EVO V2 CPU Air Cooler with SickleFlow 120, PWM Fan, Direct Contact Technology, 4 Copper Heat Pipes for AMD Ryzen/Intel LGA1700/1200/1151, Silver/Black

D-Link Day & Night Wi-Fi Camera with Remote Viewing (DCS-932L) (Discontinued by Manufacturer) First of all, the D-Link camera is relatively easy to set up - always the one to play with techie stuff first, my husband had it up and running in a flash (well almost a flash). Just attach the supplied cable to your computer, run the CD and follow the simple instructions and you're good to go. According to the instructions, you have two options to set up the camera: wirelessly or wired. Naturally, my husband tried the wireless option first, which didn't work because it claimed (spuriously, we believe) that it couldn't find the network, so he had to resort to the other method, which worked right away. We're using a Linksys wireless router.

The camera works quite well indoors where the intensity of the ambient light is generally much lower than outdoors. However, in the brighter outdoor light it is difficult to discern what you're looking at (is it a bird, is it a plane?). The colour is not the best, but then again, it ain't a Nikon 7000. There is some amount of adjustment that can be done online to change the settings, but you'll need to create an online account/register your camera first with D-Link at [...] This is also necessary if you want to view your camera remotely. Strange enough, whenever I try to access the camera online, I get a message telling me that the application needs an earlier version of Java. However, after hitting <Run> for the next three dialogue boxes or so that pop up, it will display the picture. I tried accessing the camera from outside my home network but was unable to do so. Maybe firewall issues?? (Too much effort required to check this). There is also an iPod app that is quite good, minus sound.

Night vision was surprisingly good too. In the dark, the images were shades of grey, but in brighter conditions, the colour returned. Four LED lights lit up whenever the night vision was activated (could be an issue if you wanted to place it somewhere discrete).

On the down side, the camera has to be plugged into an electrical socket to work, and the cord it came with is very short. This means you have to either place it near an electrical outlet or use an extension cord. This would obviously have limitations on where you can place it. It also has to be connected to your home network whether wired or wireless.

While in theory it could be used as a security camera, it has to be powered 24/7, so if you live in a country or area prone to an uneven power supply which could damage sensitive equipment, then you may want to consider that before getting it or you may need to install additional equipment such as line conditioners/UPS to protect your equipment.

The sound is not very good. In fact, after a few hours use it started to make a clicking sound in an endless loop.

Recommended for limited applications such as keeping an eye on kids (or pets, or pesky guests), or when you're avoiding (hiding from) certain people who come calling at your gate, but not as a dedicated security system.

Amanda Richards, June 29, 2011
text_fidelity_b: D-Link Day & Night Wi-Fi Camera with Remote Viewing (DCS-932L) (Discontinued by Manufacturer)

Ritz Gear 64GB High-Speed SDXC UHS-II SD Card, C10, U3, V90, Full-HD & 8K Memory Card for DSLR, Cinema-Quality Video Cameras This is a great card if you have a reader and/or camera compatible with the newer UHS-II format. I shoot a lot of 4k video on Sony cameras, so I very much appreciate being able to copy lots of high bitrate footage after a shoot VERY quickly, which is exactly what this does!
You can always spot the UHS-II cards by their extra pins on the back. With a reader that can utilize them, I found this card performed pretty excellent in my benchmarks! 257MB/s read and a whopping 248MB/s write! That's incredible speed for write, I wasn't expecting it. On my other cards, UHS-II boosted the read times to similar proportions but write was similar to regular U3 class SDXC cards. That this Ritz card can produce similar write times as the boosted read is pretty incredible! This might be my new favorite media.
